newsitem.title: USA: Cold, moisture push Montana plantings behind norm.
newsitem.headline: Cold, moisture push Montana plantings behind norm.

text.p: Cold temperatures and wet soils kept spring planting in Montana far behind normal in the week ended April 20, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop update.
It said 2.7 days were suitable for fieldwork in the week.

Wind damage to winter wheat was reported 62 percent light, 15 percent moderate and one percent heavy. Freeze damage to winter wheat was rated 31 percent none, 48 percent light, 15 percent moderate and six percent heavy. Winter wheat statewide was rated 41 percent good to excellent, 44 fair, 14 poor.
Spring wheat planted 5 pct vs 1 week agao, 2 year ago, 19 on a five-year average.
Barley planted 6 pct vs 2 w/a, 2 y/a, 23 avge.
Oats planted 2 pct vs 0 w/a, 5 y/a, 15 avge.
Sugar beets planted 6 pct vs 0 w/a, 8 y/a, 31 avge.
